clue.text: Sailor on ship outside Dover, say, with extremely elegant clothing

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it, so the sailor comes after the ship
the ship's letters sit outside the port, wrapping round it

parts.note: SS is the usual abbreviation for steamship
Dover is an example of a port, signalled by 'say'
Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a traditional name for a sailor

indicators.note: the extremes of the word elegant are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A sailor stepping ashore at Dover in a smart outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor on ship' reads as one picture, but in an across clue 'on' means the sailor comes after; 'outside' wraps the ship round the port, and 'extremely' takes the outer letters of 'elegant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweed blazer worn casually is a garment, an item of menswear, so clothing fits.

clue.text: Misfortune that TV repairman may bring?

definitions.meaning: a reverse or a blow to progress

explanation.surface: Bad luck that comes with the TV engineer's visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse in fortune is a misfortune; literally the returned television.

clue.text: Going to pen very small letter

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: something going is on, as in a machine left on
micro means very small

explanation.surface: Setting off to write a tiny note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like writing but means enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fifteenth character of the Greek alphabet, a short o, so a letter.

clue.text: Father and mother briefly land abroad

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are mixed up
briefly says mother loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Dad and Mum briefly touch down overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims mother to MOTHE; 'abroad' rearranges MOTHE and LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: It is informal slang for one's dad, or for a husband.

clue.text: Jay heard parrots and larks

indicators.note: heard says the word is the spoken name of a letter

parts.note: jay is how the letter J is said
to parrot is to ape or mimic

explanation.surface: Birds in the aviary: a jay listening to parrots and larks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jay' is the bird in the surface but the spoken letter J here.
explanation.definitionFit: Larks are pranks or bits of fun, and so are practical jokes of this kind.

clue.text: US gents, perhaps, determined to get honesty

parts.note: can is American slang for a toilet, such as a gents
dour can mean stern and determined

explanation.surface: American men determined to be honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gents' is a British word for a men's toilet; the US slang word for a toilet is CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankness and openness of speech are what this word means, a synonym of honesty.

clue.text: Peak always topped others

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: topped means beheaded, so the word for others loses its first letter

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A mountain peak has always been higher than the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' looks like 'surpassed' but means beheaded: REST loses R to give EST.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest mountain is a specific peak in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Doctor Aquinas busily seeing off a foreign adventurer

indicators.note: busily says the letters are set to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor called Aquinas bustling about saying goodbye to a visiting explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing off a' removes one A from DOCTOR AQUINAS before 'busily' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish conquerors of the Americas were soldier-adventurers abroad, hence foreign adventurer.

clue.text: Giant in old hat moans audibly

parts.note: something old hat is unfashionable, i.e. out

indicators.note: audibly says the word for moans is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: moans can be sighs, which said aloud gives the spelling ending this word

explanation.surface: A giant sitting in a dated hat and groaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audibly' turns SIGHS into its sound-alike SIZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra-large clothing ranges are labelled this way, so a giant item is the adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Decline to admit major sight problem

indicators.note: admitting lets the major's letters inside the decline's

parts.note: to pine is to decline or waste away
a major is a musical key, as in D major

explanation.surface: Refusing to own up to a serious eyesight problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like 'refuse' but is the verb meaning to fade away; 'major' is the musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjunctivitis is commonly called by this name, an infection that reddens the eye and troubles vision.

clue.text: Researcher's former name required, transiting border

definitions.note: Researcher's is read as Researcher is, the apostrophe-s a link

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the name's letter passes through, sitting within, the border

parts.note: a perimeter is a border

explanation.surface: A scientist's old name is needed to cross a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transiting' puts N inside PERIMETER.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who carries out trials and tests is a researcher.

clue.text: A bishop brought in to suppress endless feud

indicators.note: brought in to says the bishop and A go inside the following word
endless means the final letter of the word for suppress is dropped

parts.note: to quell is to suppress
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A bishop is called in to end a long-running feud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppress' looks like part of the bishop's job, but it is the container; 'endless' trims its last letter and 'brought in to' sets the A and Right Reverend inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A feud is a bitter dispute, and a row or dispute is the plain synonym.

clue.text: Support unruly horse (mounted)

indicators.note: unruly says the letters of horse refuse to stay in order

parts.note: someone mounted is up on a horse

explanation.surface: Holding up a wild horse with a rider on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges HORSE as SHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up or reinforce something, as with timber against a wall, is to support it.

clue.text: Definitely settle at home with family

parts.note: someone at home is in
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Deciding for good to settle down at home with the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing a date in pen rather than pencil makes an arrangement firm, an idiom for fixing it.

clue.text: Presiding officer, a Marxist, driven round in car

indicators.note: in puts the turned-round pieces inside the car's letters

parts.note: motor is an informal word for car

indicators.note: driven round says a and the Marxist are turned back to front

parts.note: a red is a communist or Marxist

explanation.surface: A communist chairman being chauffeured in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driven round' turns A plus the Marxist back to front, giving DERA, and 'in' sets that within the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair of a debate or a church assembly who keeps order is a presiding officer.

clue.text: Confuse Democrat with Tories in Barking

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: A Democrat and some Conservatives baffled in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' is a London district in the surface but means mad here.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone lose their bearings is to confuse or bewilder them.

clue.text: Primarily top dogs eat it in great quantities

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of top
the dogs eat, taking the next piece inside them

parts.note: hounds are dogs
it is sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: The best dogs wolf down their food in enormous amounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal (SA) is an old crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers in the many hundreds or more describe very large amounts, so this plural fits.

clue.text: Controlled series of balls leading to a wicket

indicators.note: leading to puts the overs before the rest in this down clue

parts.note: in cricket each over is a series of six balls, and series can be plural
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A bowler's overs culminate in a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise or manage something is to have controlled it.

clue.text: Length of life that is left for King Charles, maybe

parts.note: a life span is the length of a life

explanation.surface: How long a monarch has left to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Charles' looks royal but is a breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The King Charles is a breed of toy dog, an example of this gundog family.

clue.text: Flourish, due to return of low pound

indicators.note: return of says the low and pound letters are read backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle
LB is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: A boom thanks to a weak currency coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the cow's call, not 'weak'; MOOLB reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom or thrive, like a plant in flower, is to flourish.

clue.text: Courageous show's well done, publicity included

indicators.note: included says the publicity goes within the cry

parts.note: bravo is a cry of well done
an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A brave performance gets praise and press attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A swaggering display of boldness, often meant to impress, is a courageous show.

clue.text: Opening agency, fellow leaves for Rhode Island

indicators.note: leaves for says one letter departs and another takes its place

parts.note: an office can be an agency or bureau
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A fellow quits an agency, departing for an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: One F in OFFICE becomes RI; 'leaves for' looks like travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole or aperture, especially in the body, is an opening.

clue.text: Reactionary assembly, grim for its time

indicators.note: for its says the next word replaces a letter of the assembly

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in the Diet of Worms
grim and hard both mean harsh or severe

explanation.surface: A right-wing parliament, too bleak for the era it sits in.
explanation.walkthrough: In DIET, T (time) is swapped for HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncompromising conservative who resists all change is a reactionary.

clue.text: Studying sound of spring?

definitions.meaning: to be taking a subject, as in a degree in history
the twang a coiled spring makes when released

explanation.surface: Revising while listening to a bouncing coil.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a subject at school is studying it; the twang is a coil spring's noise.

clue.text: Concrete marker with singular omission put straight again

parts.note: something concrete is real, not abstract

indicators.note: omission says the singular letter is left out of the marker

parts.note: a sign is a marker
S abbreviates singular in grammar

explanation.surface: A concrete post with a word missing from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' is the adjective 'real', not the building material.
explanation.definitionFit: To line things up once more is to put them straight again, a re- verb.

clue.text: Italian scoring from cross in International

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An Italian footballer scoring off a cross in an international match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoring' is writing music, not goals.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was an Italian composer, someone scoring operas such as The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Devious setter's after free backing

indicators.note: after puts the setter's piece behind the turned-round one
backing says the word for free is read from the back

parts.note: to save is to rescue or free
the setter's has means I have, contracted to I've

explanation.surface: A setter who has been released and then turns sly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns SAVE into EVAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shifty who dodges straight answers is devious, a near synonym.

clue.text: Yarn about humorous duck leaving zoo in a run-down area

indicators.note: about says the yarn goes round the other pieces

parts.note: twine is a strong yarn
light means humorous, as in light verse

indicators.note: leaving says the duck departs from the zoo's letters

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: A funny duck escapes the zoo into a seedy neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is cricket's zero, the letter O, which 'leaving' removes once from the zoo; 'about' wraps the yarn round the humorous word and the remaining ZO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rundown, neglected urban district in decline is called by this term, often in the sense of a twilight world.
